headline: Between Sep 2024 and Jan 2026 the federal civilian workforce fell 12%, and the two largest land-management agencies by staff each lost more than a quarter of their employees. The sources tie the decline to personnel and hiring actions (deferred resignations, hiring controls, grant terminations); AI's employment effect has not been measured.
suggested_chart_form: Dot plot of percentage change by unit, one row per unit, each labeled with its own period and base; the two bound-only rows (value_pct blank, value_pct_bound -25) drawn as an open marker with an arrow, never as an exact point; no bars, no ranking across bases; table beside the chart.
source_note: Partnership for Public Service (OPM data, to Jan 2026; excludes USPS, the Foreign Service and much of the intelligence community); Inside Climate News (OPM data, Mar 6 2026); Agri-Pulse (OPM data, Jan 21 2026). Bases differ by row and must not be compared as one series; USDA OIG data reported in the press give a different USFS figure (16% in 2025) on another base. 'Largest' is by staff (BLM manages the most land). Federal figures only: they exclude Tribal, state, local, NGO and private workforces.
evidence_label: E for the values; J for the attribution sentence in the headline (sources: Inside Climate News on deferred resignations; EO 14356 on hiring controls; AmeriCorps litigation sources on grant terminations)

headline: Classical machine learning for science work is the largest type of registered AI in eleven federal environmental units (232 of the 329 use cases that report a type; 175 report none), and most use cases are not yet deployed: 61 of the 347 that report a stage are in production.
suggested_chart_form: Stacked horizontal bars by AI type (segments = development stage, Deployed first), with the 'not classified' row and the 'stage not reported' segment shown hatched and labeled; table beside the chart.
source_note: OMB 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory (README as of Apr 13 2026). Eleven environmental units, nine bureaus and two USDA mission areas, as extracted by EMST's labor-market analysis (docs/research/labor-market-ai-impact/scripts/omb_inventory_env.py): USGS 187, NOAA 157, Natural Resources and Environment 76, EPA 29, Farm Production and Conservation 20, FWS 11, BOR 8, BLM 7, BSEE 6, NPS 2, BIA 1 (EPA offices and regions pooled). 'Deployed' = development_stage 'Deployed' only; OMB's README pools deployed and piloted. NOAA's 157 records report neither a type nor a stage. Self-reported by agencies; registration is not use.
evidence_label: EMST derivation from an E source (counts and classification computed by EMST; not reviewed by a human)

headline: Species detection, remote sensing, water and fire lead federal environmental AI; none of the five use cases in NEPA, environmental review or permitting is deployed. NOAA's 157 records report no stage and are counted as not deployed or unreported.
suggested_chart_form: Horizontal bars of use cases per function family with the deployed share as a darker inner bar; families overlap (keyword-classified), so no totals row; table beside the chart.
source_note: OMB 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory, eleven environmental units (see F02); EMST keyword classification of use-case names and descriptions (a use case can fall in more than one family; the NEPA family's pattern includes the broad term 'permit'). 'Deployed' = development_stage 'Deployed' only; 'not_deployed_or_unreported' includes NOAA's 157 records, which report no stage.
evidence_label: EMST derivation from an E source (counts and classification computed by EMST; not reviewed by a human)

headline: Commercial AI tools for drafting, summarizing, writing and search are licensed at 10,000 or more users in each of the three main federal environmental departments (at USDA the only such tool is a search and knowledge-retrieval assistant; at Interior, a writing tool): availability at workforce scale, which is not the same as use.
suggested_chart_form: Small table (department x use-case category) with the license band as the cell value; no chart needed. Product names are deliberately omitted.
source_note: OMB 2025 consolidated COTS AI use cases (ombegov GitHub), rows for USDA, DOI and EPA marked in use with a band of 10,000+ licenses or users. Interior and USDA bands are department-wide, not limited to environmental staff. The keyword filter includes 'knowledge retrieval'; without it USDA would not appear, so do not describe the USDA row as a drafting or summarizing assistant. License bands are agency estimates; they measure availability, not frequency or quality of use.
evidence_label: E (external sources read; AI-agent checks recorded in the claims register; see source_ids per row)

headline: In western national-forest documents, components typed as monitoring make up about 31% of each 2012-rule document against about 3% of each 1982-rule plan, but the gap mostly reflects document type: 17 of the 36 2012-rule documents are monitoring evaluation reports and 5 are stand-alone monitoring plans. Among plan documents alone the shares are about 10% and 3%, with overlapping intervals; only 24 of the 84 older plans have any component typed as monitoring, so the older baseline is probably partly an extraction artifact.
suggested_chart_form: Paired dot plot (1982 rule vs 2012 rule) with 95% bootstrap whiskers, one row per variant, headline row first and labeled as such; component-weighted values as hollow markers; rows whose intervals overlap labeled 'not distinguishable'; table beside the chart.
source_note: OpenLMP 0.1.0 documents (catalog 2026-10-21, CC0), derived by EMST (docs/methods/scripts/wp10_lmp.py for the signal records; docs/package/report/figures/extract_openlmp_plans.py for the plan-level extract used here). Western national forests only: the comparison uses 120 USDA Forest Service documents (84 under the 1982 rule, 36 under the 2012 rule), and about 95% of all corpus components are Forest Service plans in western states. Cross-era comparison of different documents, not a time series. Each document is weighted equally (component-weighted values are a second check); 95% intervals are percentile bootstrap intervals over documents (seeded), which replace the earlier normal approximation. Document type (plan, monitoring evaluation report, stand-alone monitoring plan) is classified by EMST from catalog titles. Components are as typed or extracted by OpenLMP, whose extraction method differs by era; mentions measure what documents name, not obligations or funded work. Tribal touchpoints are excluded pending Tribal Advisory Council review.
evidence_label: EMST derivation from OpenLMP (CC0); document-type classification and sensitivity checks by EMST; not reviewed by a human

headline: Official 2025-35 projections show analytical, engineering and technician occupations growing faster than the +3.5% all-occupation average, foresters slower, and forest and conservation workers and water operators declining.
suggested_chart_form: Dot plot of projected percentage change by occupation with a vertical reference line at +3.5%; EMST's 'about average' band of +/-1 point shaded and labeled as EMST's convention; data scientists shown with an axis break and labeled 'reference, not environmental'; table beside the chart.
source_note: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Projections 2025-35 (released Aug 27 2026), Table 1.2 and Occupational Outlook Handbook pages. Projections are context, not evidence of skill change; BLS does not attribute these occupation projections to AI. The faster / about average / slower bands (+/-1 point around +3.5%) are an EMST display convention, not BLS categories. Data scientists are a reference point, not an environmental occupation. Compliance officers (13-1041) is a broad occupation, mostly outside environmental work. Wildland firefighters are not counted separately.
evidence_label: E (external sources read; AI-agent checks recorded in the claims register; see source_ids per row)

headline: In federal land agencies and conservation corps the entry rungs thinned in 2025-26: no non-fire seasonal hiring at the Forest Service in 2025, conservation internship postings down 44% on one board, and fewer than 8 in 100 federal employees under 30.
suggested_chart_form: Indicator table (one row per indicator, each with its own unit, period and scope) with a small inline bar for the percentage rows only; do not plot rows on a common axis.
source_note: National Parks Traveler (Nov 10 2025) on Conservation Job Board data; Partnership for Public Service (OPM data); Office of Rep. Neguse (press release Mar 23 2026 on a letter of Mar 18 2026) relaying USFS statements, including that the 2025 seasonal decision was due to budget constraints; Rep. Schrier et al. letter (Mar 23 2026) citing the USFS Trail Program Status Report. Each row has its own base. These signals followed personnel, hiring and grant decisions; none of these sources attributes them to AI. AmeriCorps context for the postings row: terminations were enjoined in the plaintiff states (Jun 2025), reinstatement eligibility was extended to grantees elsewhere (Jul 2025, uptake undocumented), and the Sep 2026 settlement covers FY2026 and the coalition jurisdictions only.
evidence_label: E (external sources read; AI-agent checks recorded in the claims register; see source_ids per row)

headline: EMST's registry records 50 dated policy actions in 2025-26 that changed or settled rules for review, authorization, hiring, disclosure or entry pathways (finalized, took effect, enacted, rescinded, enjoined, decided by a court, or a reinstatement offer), plus 11 other dated steps (proposals, bills, a court's grant of review); 6 more dated changes are scheduled for 2027. The timeline holds no technology-adoption data, so it cannot by itself show that policy moved faster than technology.
suggested_chart_form: Horizontal timeline with one swimlane per domain; recorded events as filled markers, scheduled dates as hollow markers, pending actions as dashed markers; status labels in text, not color alone; table beside the chart.
source_note: EMST L5 instrument registry and driver events (data/v2/instruments, data/v2/events; agent-recorded, unreviewed) filtered to events whose dates rest on verification records (V1-V4 key facts, the corrections register and the WP-15 re-checks of 2026-10-23). Filter rule: an event is admitted if all its sources are verification records, or if any source is a WP-15 re-check; some admitted events also cite a role source row that no verification pass re-checked (for example the objection-rule event cites SC-009). Two recorded events (AmeriCorps, July 2025; New Jersey Supreme Court, July 2026) come from corrected claims-register rows and are not yet in data/v2/events. Scheduled and pending items come from the same records; future dates are as of 2026-10-23 and must be re-checked. Superseded verification records are replaced by their current register rows (see SUPERSEDED_SUCCESSORS in the script). Bills are shown at their recorded stage only; none is law. Litigation outcomes after the dates shown were not checked. Held (Tribal-related) instruments excluded.
evidence_label: EMST record of external events (agent-recorded); dates checked against verification records and the claims register

headline: EMST v2's first 13 role profiles form three corridors that are designed to cross all three crafts and end in state and federal role variants; no role yet has a change indicator that has passed EMST's evidence rule.
suggested_chart_form: Three horizontal swimlanes (one per corridor) of role boxes in step order, with levels as a band inside each box and 'emerging' roles outlined dashed; a footer row per box shows 'change indicator: none active' and the count of watch signals. No craft blends or change ratings are drawn: those are agent drafts awaiting multi-rater assessment.
source_note: EMST mvp_role_set.csv (ADR-0006, a decision record drafted by EMST's AI agents) and the generated role change views (docs/build/WP-08/generated/change_view/). 'Designed to cross all three crafts' describes the corridor design; the craft ratings that would show it are agent drafts and are deliberately not charted. Indicator status is computed by the ADR-0028 evidence rule (two independent signal families, two periods, named human review); every attached signal is at watch status. Tribal variants are held and not shown.
evidence_label: Structure: EMST decision record (ADR-0006). Indicator status: computed. No agent ratings shown.
